messages:
elaine-sales: ACME follow-up - during the dry-run this morning they got a wave of 5xxs when they hammer-tested with a ramp to 200 rps. They're calling it a deal blocker unless we can promise stability for the customer demo tomorrow. Can SE + ops quick swarm?

jordan-se: Can someone drop the error samples and the client timestamps? Need request_ids to map to logs.

elaine-sales: From their client: 
```
[2026-04-02T09:18:23Z] 503 Service Unavailable - req=tx_9f8e
[2026-04-02T09:18:24Z] 502 Bad Gateway - req=tx_9f8f
```
They report the spike lasted ~4m and started 09:18 UTC during a scripted ramp.

leo-ops: infra-bot pulled metrics for project=acme-poc in eu-west-1. Summary: queue_depth hit 300, pool_capacity=0 available for model redwood-v1, autoscaler triggered but new nodes not ready until ~65s after threshold. Logs: queue_timeout -> 504.

infra-bot: ALERT: queue_depth_threshold_exceeded for acme-poc at 2026-04-02T09:18:40Z. Collected 40 log lines for tx_9f8e.

maria-runtime: Thanks - looks like two things: (1) autoscale policy is conservative (scale_threshold=70) and warm_spare=0, (2) project doesn't have burst_pool enabled so short spikes overflow queues. For a demo, short-term we can: enable burst_pool, add fallback routing to redwood-v1-quant, and increase queue_timeout.

jordan-se: Confirmed they turned off burst to avoid surprise charges. Sales asked for cost limits. We should apply a capped burst credit for the POC and notify them.

elaine-sales: They want a one-click toggle before the 11:00 call. Is there a safe sequence we can do now that minimizes risk?

leo-ops: Sequence I recommend: 1) enable burst_pool with cap=10k tokens 2) set routing fallback: on_queue>80 -> redwood-v1-quant 3) set queue_timeout=60s 4) set autoscale scale_threshold=50 and warm_spare=1. We can do 1-3 now, autoscale change should be applied but may need a config rollout.

maria-runtime: I can apply the routing and queue_timeout now. Routing command: 
```
rwctl routing add --project acme-poc --rule "queue_depth>80 => redwood-v1-quant"
rwctl config set --project acme-poc queue_timeout=60
```

jordan-se: I'll prepare a billing note to send the customer explaining burst cap behavior and that burst usage will be flagged for review. For the demo we can set the cap low.

leo-ops: Applying burst_pool enable with cap now. infra-bot: record change.

infra-bot: CONFIG: burst_pool=enabled cap=10000 tokens for project=acme-poc by leo-ops at 2026-04-02T09:26:05Z

maria-runtime: Routing + timeout applied. Recommend we run a controlled verification: a 3-minute ramp to 180 rps from a staging runner to validate no queue drops. I'll kick that off in 5m and post results.

elaine-sales: Please also capture request_ids during the test so we can show ACME the logs if they ask. They specifically want to know what happens when the autoscaler is slow.

jordan-se: I'll add a temporary dashboard snapshot and a note in the POC billing sheet about burst costs and how to change caps.

maria-runtime: One more note: for longer-term we should offer them a Dedicated trial with warm_spare and guaranteed demo window SLA. For now these mitigations will keep the demo stable.

leo-ops: Follow-ups: enable alerting on queue_depth>200 with pager enabled, add a short playbook to the POC doc describing the mitigation steps (routing fallback, burst cap, autoscale tweak).

elaine-sales: Great work team. I'll update ACME and ask if they want the capped burst enabled permanently for the trial. If they sign, we can discuss converting to a reserved capacity pilot.

jordan-se: If we see any new 5xxs, paste request_ids here and escalate to runtime oncall.

elaine-sales: Closing for now. Will report back after the verification run. :rocket:
